newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces four new ambassadorial nominees.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces four new ambassadorial nominees.

text.p: President Bill Clinton announced his nominations on Monday for ambassadors to Paraguay, Colombia, Belarus and the Kyrgyz Republic.
All the nominees require Senate confirmation.
For Paraguay, Clinton nominated Maura Harty, a career foreign service member who was most recently executive assistant to Warren Christopher when he was secretary of state.
Clinton nominated Warren Kamman, a career foreign service member, to be ambassador to Colombia. He is current U.S. ambassador to Bolivia.
For Belarus, Clinton chose Daniel Speckhard, who since 1993 has been a deputy ambassador-at-large to the states newly independent from the former Soviet Union.
Clinton picked Anne Marie Sigmund, a career foreign service member who is currently counsellor of the U.S. Information Agency, to be U.S. ambassador for the Kyrgyz Republic.
In another move, Clinton nominated Wendy Ruth Sherman to be counsellor of the State Department with the rank of ambassador. She is currently president of the Fannie Mae Foundation.
The announcements were made in Boston where Clinton was on a fund-raising trip.
